offences.quote: Copying and pasting chunks of text generated by an AI tool into your assessment is plagiarism.
If your assessment contains fabricated data, this is regarded as academic misconduct.
Use paraphrasing tools to rewrite material someone else has written and copy it into your text. Submitting this as your own work is plagiarism.
if the tool is used to generate work that is not your own and which you do not disclose, this may be regarded as a breach of academic integrity.

liability.quote: We know that it takes time to understand what is acceptable in academic writing and that sometimes students make mistakes

detection.quote: If we are concerned that your assignment relies too heavily on AI, or contains inaccuracies as a result of using AI, we may invite you to explain your work.
If we are concerned that your assignment relies too heavily on AI, or contains inaccuracies as a result of using AI, we may invite you to explain your work.
Telling us how you developed your argument and showing your drafts, notes and summaries of readings and journal articles helps us understand that your work is not AI-generated.

process.quote: being asked to discuss your assignment is not an allegation of academic misconduct or that you breached academic integrity

Where the course coordinator believes that the way you have used AI is a breach of academic integrity, they may deal with the case as Poor Academic Practice or refer the case to the Academic Integrity Officer to deal with it as a Minor Breach or Academic Misconduct.
